narrative:
Your loan application was carefully reviewed, and the assessment found a 59% likelihood that you represent a credit risk — a figure that, while not overwhelmingly high, was sufficient to result in a denial. This means the decision was not clear-cut, and your profile contains both concerning and reassuring elements that pulled the outcome in different directions.

The single most influential factor working against your application was the current status of your checking account, which shows a negative balance. Among applicants who were approved, only about one in five had a checking account in the red, and having no positive buffer in your account signals to the assessment that your day-to-day finances may already be under strain before taking on any new debt. This was the strongest signal pushing your application toward denial, and it carried more weight than any other aspect of your profile.

On a more positive note, your savings situation actually worked in your favor to some degree. Although your savings are listed as unknown or none — a category shared by roughly one in five approved applicants — the model interpreted this in a way that slightly offset the concerns raised by your checking account. This is a nuanced point: the absence of recorded savings did not dramatically hurt you here, and in fact provided a small counterbalancing effect.

However, the purpose of your loan — purchasing a new car — added further pressure toward denial. While nearly one in five approved applicants also sought financing for a new car, this purpose tends to be associated with higher risk compared to, say, financing household electronics or furniture, and it reinforced the concerns already raised by your account status.

Beyond these top three factors, a few other aspects of your profile are worth noting. Your requested loan duration of 24 months is somewhat longer than the average of about 19 months among approved applicants, and your installment repayment rate is set at the highest tier, meaning a larger share of your disposable income would go toward repayments — both of which add financial pressure. You are also renting your home, whereas the vast majority of approved applicants own their residence, which further limits the financial security signals in your profile.

To improve your chances in the future, the most impactful step would be to bring your checking account into a positive balance and maintain it there for a sustained period before reapplying. Reducing the installment rate by requesting a smaller loan amount or extending repayment terms could also help, as could building up documented savings. If the car purchase is urgent, you might also explore whether a used car — which tends to be viewed more favorably — could meet your needs at a lower loan amount.
